transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-25 14:00 PDT — Duration 48m. Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (CTO), Marcus (ML Eng), Priya (Infra)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick intro — I'm Samira, AE at Redwood Infer — Redwood Inference, yes sorry — and this is Diego our SE.
[00:10] Lena: Hi, thanks. We were excited to talk through the credits path and what 'time to first token' really looks like.
[00:18] Diego: great, can you give a quick context on what you're building and the main constraint?
[00:25] Marcus: Sure, we're building a near-real-time summarization pipeline for streaming logs — low-latency is important but cost matters, we expect lots of short requests.
[00:35] Priya: from infra side we're evaluating whether hosted is fine or we need VPC/on-prem due to residency and KMS integration.
[00:45] Samira: awesome. high-level: we offer self-serve credits to get you to first token fast, usually a few hours to a day to redeem and prototype. The hosted API is fastest TTFT; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and Reserved capacity, and Private is for VPC/air-gapped.
[01:05] Lena: what is the typical flow for credits? like how do engineers actually spin up something?
[01:12] Samira: you redeem credits in-console, you get API keys, we have SDKs and a quickstart repo. Diego, can you walk the dev path?
[01:20] Diego: yeah, normally devs pull our quickstart, drop in their prompt set, and call the /generate endpoint. For short requests we recommend models with optimized kernel picks and sometimes int8 quant for cost. You'll see latency numbers in the perf sheet.
[01:37] Marcus: any chance for streaming? our app benefits from partial responses.
[01:41] Diego: yes, streaming is supported on hosted and dedicated, for private it depends on your network config but we can enable. Streaming does slightly change batching behavior.
[01:50] [01:51] Lena: Can you explain dedicated vs private? They sound similar.
[01:56] Samira: dedicated = reserved GPU pools in our infra, customer-isolated tenancy and commit contracts. private = customer-managed control plane or VPC connectors, can be on-prem or in a customer VPC, full KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.
[02:12] Priya: For KMS — do you support external key stores / HSM? We need to bring our keys.
[02:17] Diego: yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. Dedicated can integrate with KMS with some config; Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default but we offer envelope encryption options.
[02:28] Marcus: latency numbers — do you have baseline for our use case? short prompts, 150 tokens avg.
[02:35] Diego: rough hosted baseline for a 150-token gen on a mid-sized model is ~120-170ms p50, p95 around 350-500ms depending on sequence length and batch. With dedicated we can push p95 lower — depends on GPU type and continuous batching.
[02:52] Lena: those p95 ranges are big. what's the knob for consistency?
[02:57] Diego: reserved capacity, strict autoscaling policies, and limiting batch windows. Also prefix/KV caching for repeated context reduces downstream token work.
[03:08] [03:09] Priya: what about regulatory — SOC2, ISO, audit logs?
[03:13] Samira: we are SOC two Type II certified — customers sometimes call it SOC2 — and have ISO in progress. For Private we provide detailed audit logs and per-token lineage if needed.
[03:26] Marcus: how common is it that teams start with hosted credits then move to dedicated?
[03:30] Samira: very common PLG path: self-serve hosted credits to validate metrics and UX, then move to Dedicated as traffic and SLOs require predictability, then Private if compliance or data residency demands it.
[03:44] Lena: does the quickstart include a cost estimator so engineers can see per-call cost with batching?
[03:48] Diego: yes, our quickstart includes a token-cost calculator, and our Optimize toolkit suggests batching and quantization configs. We'll share a spreadsheet showing cost per 10k calls across configs.
[04:01] [04:03] Marcus: what about rate limits and throttling in hosted?
[04:06] Samira: hosted has tiered rate limits; you get generous limits with credits but at scale we recommend Dedicated. We also support per-route quotas and graceful fallbacks to cheaper model variants.
[04:17] Priya: data retention — logs and prompts — how long do you keep them in hosted?
[04:21] Diego: default retention is 30 days for analytics and logs, but you can opt-out or request deletion; Private gives you full control. We'll include our data retention policy doc.
[04:33] Lena: ok great. I want to understand how long it will take our team to validate the pipeline end-to-end with your credits.
[04:40] Samira: typical is 1-2 weeks for a minimal TTFT sprint if you have sample prompts. If you want lower p95 consistency and real-traffic benchmarks, 2-4 weeks with a small pilot.
[04:51] [05:00] Marcus: our developers prefer examples for batcher configs; they use variable size batches.
[05:05] Diego: we can share recommended batching policies and a sample autoscaler config for Docker/K8s. Note: continuous batching in our runtime tries to balance latency and throughput; you can tune via batch window and max tokens.
[05:22] Lena: security stakeholders will ask about SSO/SCIM and RBAC; do you support enterprise SSO?
[05:28] Samira: yes, SSO with SAML/SCIM, RBAC, and per-team project isolation are supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports SSO for orgs too.
[05:38] Priya: for the Private deployment, can we run the control plane in our VPC and still use Redwood for model updates?
[05:44] Diego: yes, our Private offering lets you keep a control plane in your VPC and we can push model artifacts via signed bundles. There's an offline install option for air-gapped environments too.
[05:58] [06:00] Lena: great. Are there any gotchas when starting with credits we should warn our engs about?
[06:05] Samira: a few: 1) tokenization differences across model families (so prompt engineering matters), 2) latency variance during cold starts or when autoscaling, 3) if you need KMS bring-your-own, hosted won't satisfy that. We'll call these out.
[06:21] Marcus: on tokenization — will the quickstart show the exact token counts we should expect?
[06:26] Diego: yes, the sample script prints token counts and effective cost per call.
[06:30] [06:35] Lena: about benchmarking — can the SE run a small perf test against our sample prompts?
[06:39] Diego: absolutely. If you share 50–100 representative prompts we can run hosted and dedicated runs and surface p50/p95, cost per token, and memory/KV usage.
[06:50] Priya: network egress — if we use hosted, what are egress implications?
[06:54] Samira: egress depends on region; we'll share region-specific notes. For large payloads we recommend compressing and trimming context.
[07:06] [07:15] Marcus: competitor question — some vendors advertise sub-100ms p95.
[07:19] Diego: marketing numbers vary; we publish benchmark methodology. Real p95 depends a lot on prompt length, concurrency pattern and GPU type. We prefer to benchmark with your data.
[07:32] Lena: what's the handoff if we decide to go Dedicated after credits? procurement steps?
[07:36] Samira: we'll issue a Dedicated proposal with capacity tiers and commit terms. Procurement will request standard security addenda; we have a starter enterprise contract and an SOW for Dedicated.
[07:47] [07:50] Priya: do you provide dashboards for per-token cost and tracing?
[07:53] Diego: yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency dashboards, and distributed tracing hooks. You can export traces to your observability stack.
[08:05] Marcus: one more — do you support function calling or structured outputs?
[08:09] Diego: yes, we support structured output and function/tool calling primitives on the API.
[08:14] [08:20] Samira: ok let's recap action items and next steps. We'll send: quickstart guide + redemption link, a perf spreadsheet, and a one-pager on security/compliance. We want your sample prompts and a follow-up technical deep dive next week.
[08:33] Lena: sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:36] Diego: no blockers — just waiting on sample prompts and any special compliance forms.
[08:40] Priya: I'll check with legal and add compliance contacts.
[08:44] [08:50] Marcus: timeline — if we get started tomorrow with credits, when can we expect first data?
[08:54] Samira: you can be calling the API in hours after redeeming credits and running the quickstart. Real benchmarks in 2–5 days depending on scheduling.
[09:03] Lena: ok thanks everyone. We'll look out for the email.

End of meeting — 48m total.

Notes on transcript quality: automated engine made a few mis-hearings (Redwood Infer vs Redwood Inference), some technical terms like K/V cache transcribed as K V cash in places. There were brief cross-talks and filler words left in to preserve authenticity.
